name: MONACO

flag.title: Red & White
flag.note: Red over white — Grimaldi colours since 1339

lead: Monaco is a tiny country ruled by a prince. It is squeezed between France and the sea. The Grimaldi family has ruled this cliff since 1297. It has a grand casino and a Formula One street race.
geo: Monaco clings to a limestone cliff on the French Riviera. It is barely bigger than New York's Central Park. You can walk across it in 20 minutes.
The harbour, Port Hercule, fills with the world's largest superyachts each spring. Engineers have built new land out into the sea, so Monaco grows a little each year.
animals: Octopus, sea bream, and moray eels hide below the harbour. Striped dolphins and fin whales pass by each summer.
The yellow-legged gull rules the rooftops. The blind Mediterranean mole finds its way by touch under the soil.
culture: Monaco mixes French style with Italian warmth. The national dish is barbajuan, a crispy fried parcel of chard and ricotta. The ballet, orchestra, and opera all share one grand theatre.
Every May, the Monaco Grand Prix turns the streets into a racing circuit. Only about a quarter of residents are native Monegasques. The law bans them from gambling in the casino.
history: In 1297, François Grimaldi dressed as a monk and tricked his way into Monaco's fortress. He hid a sword under his robe. His family still holds the rock.
By the 1860s, Monaco was nearly bankrupt. Prince Charles III opened the Monte-Carlo Casino in 1863, and wealthy gamblers flooded in. By 1869 he had ended income tax.
wows: Monaco is the world's most crowded country, with over 18,000 people per km².
The law bans Monegasque citizens from gambling in the Monte-Carlo Casino.
Prince Charles III ended income tax in 1869, and it never came back.
The Monaco Grand Prix has used the same streets since 1929.
Monaco has zero public debt, so it owes nothing.
Fontvieille district sits entirely on land built out into the sea.
Ayrton Senna won the Monaco Grand Prix six times, a record.

myths.fact: Monaco has only a heliport. Helicopters fly there from Nice airport in about seven minutes.
Monaco is its own country, with its own flag and laws. It joined the United Nations in 1993.
